subject: general
question: An adult human urine consists of:

options.text: 95% water, 2.5% urea and 2.5% other waste products

solution:
The correct answer is __**95% water, 2.5% urea and 2.5% other waste products**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, two ureters, a urinary bladder, and a urethra.
 
• The kidney initiates the formation of urine, and the urethra facilitates urine excretion.
 
• Humans are ureotelic, and excretion occurs in the form of urea, resulting in less loss of body water.
 
• Kidneys are reddish-brown, bean-shaped structures. An adult human kidney measures 10-12cm in length, 5-7cm in width, and 2-3cm in thickness, with an average weight of 12-170gm.
 
• Through nephrons (tiny filtering units), the kidneys remove waste products called urea, as well as extra water and ions from the blood to form urine.
 
• The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney.
 
• The pelvis of the kidney is continued as a ureter. 
 
• The ureter is a long and muscular tube.
 
• The ureter carries urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
 
• In the pelvic cavity, there is a thin-walled, pear-shaped, white transparent sac called the urinary bladder.
 
• It temporarily stores the urine.
 
• The urethra is a membranous tube that arises from the urinary bladder.
 
• The urethra conducts urine to the exterior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e41f1740cdb8115a19d9bbfcf5e898af70219f2d79922d8483412abbbc330bb3.png] 

Thus, the Correct path of urine in our body is Kidney → ureter → urinary bladder → urethra.__
